messages.subject: stationary distribution for HMM
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to fit a hidden markov model in which it would make
sense to suppose that the initial latent values were drawn from a
the stationary distribution of the latent transition matrix P.

I am wondering how to calculate that in Stan -- I know various
ways of doing this, but I want it to play nice with autodiff and I
have never thought about it in this context, so I don't know the
pitfalls.

I know that P is irreducible.

Suggestions, references to examples, etc are appreciated.

Best,

Tamas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stationary distribution for HMM
parts:
I'm afraid Stan can only compute eigenvectors of symmetric
matrices (otherwise we have issues with possibly complex results).

Is there another way to do this calculation? You could
probably do it approximately by multiplying the matrix a few times.

- Bob

messages.author: 1f723d378f24adbb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stationary distribution for HMM
parts:
Eigenvectors are overkill. For a given matrix P,

p P = p
p 1 = 1

is a linear problem (the 1 on the LHS is a vector, on the RHS a
scalar). The system is linearly dependent so you just drop one
equation from the top ones.

Thinking about this, I see no reason why this should not work
(continuous and differentiable a.a. for P). But since I have a
small sparse system, I ended up calculating the steady state in
Maxima, and copy-pasting that in to Stan, and it works fine.

(Since #680 is still unresolved, I ended up doing the same for a
matrix exponential.)

Best,

Tamas
